null_email_assertion.after_sql: INSERT INTO public.users(id,username) VALUES ('{extra}','audit_null_one'),('{missing}','audit_null_two');DO $check$ BEGIN IF ((SELECT count(*)=2 FROM public.users WHERE id IN ('{extra}','{missing}') AND email IS NULL)) IS NOT TRUE THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'ASSERTION: Expected database state was not observed'; END IF; END $check$;
null_email_assertion.rationale: Observe the two newly inserted users. Shared seed users have their emails deliberately changed while preparing the NULLS NOT DISTINCT index mutant, so seed-only preparation could falsify the old assertion without defective uniqueness enforcement.

Adjacent lifecycle preservation checks may share boundary observations while retaining every transition gate; no changes made here.
Same kill sets do not prove Unicode inputs redundant; all remaining distinct Unicode cases preserved.

backup_overlap_review.rationale: Source baselines use rollback-only fixtures, including actual second-write FK failure and reconnect. Preparation may run concurrently using WAL-complete fresh pg_basebackup and pg_verifybackup, but fault isolation controls themselves inject faults and must wait until both baseline stages finish. Copy startup must independently verify recovery completion, identity, data directory, empty rows, schema fingerprint and durable server settings; join startup before cleanup on any failure.
backup_overlap_review.limitation: pg_verifybackup is not a complete restoration proof. No runtime benchmark was performed by this reviewer.
